qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is NOT transmitted through a mosquito bite?

text_solutions: Amoebiasis is caused by Entamoeba histolytica and is transmitted through contaminated food and water, not mosquitoes.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a preventive measure against vector-borne diseases?

text_solutions: Using mosquito nets, repellents, and eliminating stagnant water help prevent vector-borne diseases like malaria and dengue.

qns_content.text: Which type of cells produce antibodies in the human body?

text_solutions: B-lymphocytes differentiate into plasma cells, which produce antibodies for immune responses.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the main causative agent of the common cold?

text_solutions: Rhinoviruses are the most common causative agents of the common cold.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of malignant tumors?

options.text: Presence of a capsule around the tumor

text_solutions: Malignant tumors exhibit uncontrolled growth and have the ability to metastasize, spreading to other parts of the body.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the causative agent of cholera?

text_solutions: Cholera is caused by Vibrio cholerae, a bacterium that spreads through contaminated water and food.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about passive immunity is correct?

options.text: Passive immunity involves the production of memory cells.

text_solutions: Passive immunity provides short-term protection as it involves the transfer of ready-made antibodies rather than immune system activation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about cell-mediated immunity is correct?

options.text: Cytotoxic T-cells play a key role in cell-mediated immunity.
Cell-mediated immunity involves the production of antibodies.
Cell-mediated immunity does not target virus-infected cells.

text_solutions: Cell-mediated immunity is primarily carried out by cytotoxic T-cells, which attack virus-infected and cancerous cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the adaptive immune system is correct?

options.text: The adaptive immune system provides a non-specific response.
The adaptive immune system does not involve memory cells.
The adaptive immune system includes B-lymphocytes and T-lymphocytes.
The adaptive immune system acts immediately without prior exposure.

text_solutions: The adaptive immune system involves B-lymphocytes and T-lymphocytes, providing a specific response and memory against pathogens.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a bacterial disease?

text_solutions: Common cold is caused by rhinoviruses, whereas typhoid, pneumonia, and diphtheria are bacterial infections.

qns_content.text: Which of the following substances is classified as a hallucinogen?

text_solutions: Cannabinoids, obtained from Cannabis sativa, are hallucinogens that affect the central nervous system.

qns_content.text: What is the primary function of lymph nodes in the immune system?

options.text: Filtration of lymph and activation of immune cells

text_solutions: Lymph nodes filter lymph, trap pathogens, and activate immune cells such as lymphocytes.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the best way to prevent dengue fever?

text_solutions: Dengue is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, so eliminating stagnant water where mosquitoes breed is the best preventive measure.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about interferons is TRUE?

options.text: They are used for treating bacterial infections
They help protect cells from viral infections

text_solutions: Interferons are proteins produced by virus-infected cells to prevent the spread of viral infections.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by a protozoan?

text_solutions: Amoebiasis is caused by the protozoan Entamoeba histolytica, which infects the intestine.

qns_content.text: Which organ is responsible for the production of T-lymphocytes?

text_solutions: The thymus is the primary organ responsible for the maturation of T-lymphocytes.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about cancer is incorrect?

options.text: Cancer cells lose the property of contact inhibition.
Cancer cells always remain localized and do not spread.

text_solutions: Cancer cells can metastasize, meaning they spread to other tissues and organs through the blood and lymphatic system.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about autoimmune diseases is incorrect?

options.text: Autoimmune diseases occur when the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
Autoimmune diseases can affect multiple organs in the body.
Autoimmune diseases are caused by bacterial infections.

text_solutions: Autoimmune diseases are not caused by bacterial infections; they result from immune system dysfunction.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about passive immunity is incorrect?

options.text: Passive immunity is acquired through the transfer of antibodies.
Passive immunity can be provided by maternal antibodies.

text_solutions: Passive immunity does not involve memory cell formation; it provides temporary protection using ready-made antibodies.

qns_content.text: Which type of immunity is provided by vaccination?

text_solutions: Vaccination stimulates the immune system to produce a memory response, providing active immunity.

qns_content.text: Which cells act as the first line of defense in innate immunity?

text_solutions: Macrophages are phagocytic cells that act as the first line of defense in innate immunity by engulfing pathogens.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a primary lymphoid organ?

text_solutions: The thymus is a primary lymphoid organ where T-lymphocytes mature before they enter circulation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the primary function of the spleen in the immune system?

options.text: Filtration of blood and removal of old RBCs

text_solutions: The spleen filters blood, removes old red blood cells, and contains immune cells that help fight infections.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a secondary lymphoid organ?

text_solutions: The spleen is a secondary lymphoid organ where immune cells interact with antigens.

qns_content.text: Which type of immunity is acquired after recovering from a disease?

text_solutions: Active acquired immunity develops when the body produces antibodies and memory cells after recovering from an infection.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about phagocytosis is correct?

options.text: Phagocytosis is the process by which immune cells engulf and digest pathogens.
Phagocytosis occurs exclusively in the lymphatic system.
Phagocytosis is a function of red blood cells.

text_solutions: Phagocytosis is the process by which immune cells, such as macrophages and neutrophils, engulf and digest pathogens.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about antibodies is correct?

options.text: Antibodies are part of the innate immune system.

text_solutions: Plasma cells, which are differentiated B-lymphocytes, secrete antibodies to help neutralize pathogens.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about natural killer (NK) cells is correct?

options.text: NK cells are a type of T-lymphocyte.
NK cells play a role in innate immunity.

text_solutions: Natural killer (NK) cells are part of the innate immune system and help eliminate virus-infected and cancerous cells.

qns_content.text: Which disease is caused by the protozoan Entamoeba histolytica?

text_solutions: Amoebiasis, also known as amoebic dysentery, is caused by Entamoeba histolytica, a protozoan parasite.

qns_content.text: Which toxic substance in tobacco is responsible for an increased risk of lung cancer?

text_solutions: Tar, a component of tobacco smoke, contains carcinogenic substances that increase the risk of lung cancer.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the mode of action of opioids?

options.text: Binding to opioid receptors in the central nervous system

text_solutions: Opioids bind to specific opioid receptors in the central nervous system, producing pain relief and euphoria.

qns_content.text: Which disease is prevented by the MMR vaccine?

text_solutions: The MMR vaccine protects against Measles, Mumps, and Rubella.

qns_content.text: Which type of immune cells are primarily involved in destroying virus-infected cells?

text_solutions: T-cytotoxic cells (CD8+ cells) destroy virus-infected cells by inducing apoptosis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is NOT caused by a virus?

text_solutions: Diphtheria is caused by the bacterium Corynebacterium diphtheriae, whereas the others are viral diseases.

qns_content.text: Which type of T-lymphocyte suppresses immune responses to prevent excessive reactions?

text_solutions: Regulatory T-cells (Tregs) help suppress excessive immune responses to maintain immune system balance.

qns_content.text: Which component of the immune system acts as the first line of defense?

text_solutions: The skin and mucous membranes act as physical barriers, providing the first line of defense against infections.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about interferons is incorrect?

options.text: Interferons help protect neighboring cells from viral infections.

text_solutions: Interferons are not antibodies; they are signaling proteins that help prevent viral replication.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about antigen-presenting cells (APCs) is incorrect?

text_solutions: Erythrocytes (red blood cells) do not function as antigen-presenting cells; APCs include macrophages and dendritic cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about vaccines is incorrect?

text_solutions: Vaccines provide **active** immunity by stimulating the immune system, not passive immunity.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an autoimmune disease?

text_solutions: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the body's own joints.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by a fungal infection?

text_solutions: Ringworm is a fungal infection caused by genera such as Microsporum, Trichophyton, and Epidermophyton.

qns_content.text: Which type of immunity is provided by colostrum to a newborn?

text_solutions: Colostrum contains maternal antibodies (IgA) that provide passive immunity to the newborn.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a bacterial disease?

text_solutions: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following pathogens causes pneumonia?

text_solutions: Pneumonia is caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, which infects the lungs and causes breathing difficulties.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a zoonotic disease?

text_solutions: Rabies is a zoonotic disease, meaning it is transmitted from animals to humans, usually through bites from infected animals.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about tuberculosis is correct?

text_solutions: Tuberculosis is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and is transmitted through airborne droplets.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about immunoglobulins (antibodies) is correct?

options.text: IgG is the most abundant antibody in blood plasma.
IgA is primarily found in the bloodstream.

text_solutions: IgG is the most abundant antibody in the blood and plays a key role in long-term immunity.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the immune system is correct?

options.text: The immune system consists only of white blood cells.
The immune system includes specialized organs, cells, and proteins.
The immune system does not recognize self and non-self.
The immune system is only active during infections.

text_solutions: The immune system consists of specialized organs (like the thymus, spleen, and lymph nodes), cells (like WBCs), and proteins that work together to defend the body.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about T-cytotoxic cells is correct?

options.text: T-cytotoxic cells are part of the innate immune system.
T-cytotoxic cells function only in allergic reactions.

text_solutions: T-cytotoxic cells (CD8+ T-cells) are responsible for identifying and destroying virus-infected and cancerous cells.

qns_content.text: Which component of tobacco causes addiction by stimulating the adrenal gland?

text_solutions: Nicotine stimulates the adrenal gland to release adrenaline, which increases heart rate and causes addiction.

qns_content.text: Which class of drugs is used as a depressant and acts on the central nervous system?

text_solutions: Opioids act as depressants on the central nervous system and slow down body functions.

qns_content.text: Which type of vaccine contains inactivated or killed pathogens?

text_solutions: Killed vaccines contain inactivated pathogens that stimulate an immune response without causing disease.

qns_content.text: Which immune cells play a major role in graft rejection?

text_solutions: T-cytotoxic cells recognize and destroy foreign graft cells, leading to graft rejection.

qns_content.text: Which type of cells produce antibodies?

text_solutions: B-lymphocytes differentiate into plasma cells, which produce antibodies.

qns_content.text: Which immune component provides the first line of defense against infections?

text_solutions: The skin and mucous membranes act as physical barriers and provide the first line of defense against infections.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about antibiotics is incorrect?

options.text: Overuse of antibiotics can lead to resistance.
Antibiotics work by inhibiting bacterial growth or killing bacteria.

text_solutions: Antibiotics are not effective against viruses; they only target bacterial infections.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about interferons is correct?

options.text: Interferons help in defending against viral infections.
Interferons are produced only in bacterial infections.

text_solutions: Interferons are signaling proteins produced by virus-infected cells to help protect neighboring cells from viral infection.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about T-helper cells is incorrect?

options.text: T-helper cells secrete cytokines to regulate immune responses.
T-helper cells play a role in adaptive immunity.

text_solutions: T-helper cells do not directly kill infected cells; they assist by activating B-cells and other immune responses.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about histamine is incorrect?

text_solutions: Histamine does not reduce inflammation; instead, it promotes inflammation and allergic responses.

qns_content.text: What is the causative agent of the common cold?

text_solutions: The common cold is primarily caused by rhinoviruses, which infect the nose and respiratory passage.

qns_content.text: Which of the following pathogens is transmitted by the tsetse fly?

text_solutions: Trypanosoma, the causative agent of sleeping sickness, is transmitted by the tsetse fly.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about mast cells is correct?

options.text: Mast cells release histamine during allergic reactions.
Mast cells are involved in oxygen transport.
Mast cells are not involved in immune responses.

text_solutions: Mast cells release histamine, which plays a key role in allergic reactions and inflammation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the most common mode of transmission of tuberculosis?

text_solutions: Tuberculosis spreads through inhalation of airborne droplets from an infected person.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a key symptom of tetanus infection?

text_solutions: Tetanus is caused by Clostridium tetani and leads to muscle stiffness and painful spasms due to toxin production.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about AIDS is correct?

options.text: AIDS is caused by a bacterial infection.
AIDS weakens the immune system by destroying CD4+ T-cells.

text_solutions: AIDS is caused by HIV, which destroys CD4+ T-cells, leading to immune system failure.

qns_content.text: What is the role of IgE antibodies?

text_solutions: IgE antibodies are involved in allergic reactions by triggering mast cells to release histamine.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the primary mode of transmission for cholera?

text_solutions: Cholera is caused by Vibrio cholerae and spreads through contaminated water and food.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about inflammation is correct?

options.text: Inflammation only occurs in response to bacterial infections.
Inflammation results in increased blood flow to affected areas.
Inflammation has no role in tissue repair.
Inflammation prevents immune cells from reaching infection sites.

text_solutions: Inflammation increases blood flow to infected or injured areas, helping immune cells reach and eliminate pathogens.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about lymph is correct?

options.text: Lymph is a fluid that circulates only in blood vessels.
Lymph carries white blood cells and helps in immune responses.

text_solutions: Lymph is a fluid that carries white blood cells and helps in immune responses by transporting immune cells and nutrients.

qns_content.text: Which immune cells are primarily responsible for phagocytosis?

text_solutions: Macrophages are phagocytic cells that engulf and destroy pathogens, playing a key role in innate immunity.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the causative agent of filariasis?

text_solutions: Filariasis is caused by the filarial worm Wuchereria bancrofti, which affects the lymphatic system.

qns_content.text: Which of the following pathogens is associated with causing whooping cough?

text_solutions: Whooping cough is caused by Bordetella pertussis, which affects the respiratory system.

qns_content.text: Which antibody is predominantly present in colostrum and helps in passive immunity of newborns?

text_solutions: IgA is the predominant antibody in colostrum and provides passive immunity to newborns.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by a prion?

text_solutions: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) is caused by prions, which are misfolded proteins that damage the nervous system.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a function of the lymphatic system?

options.text: Removal of interstitial fluid and immune function

text_solutions: The lymphatic system removes interstitial fluid, transports lymphocytes, and helps in immune defense.

qns_content.text: Which fungal infection affects the skin, nails, and scalp?

text_solutions: Ringworm is a fungal infection caused by species of Microsporum, Trichophyton, and Epidermophyton.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the inflammatory response is correct?

options.text: Inflammation decreases blood flow to the affected area.
Inflammation always causes harm to the body.
Inflammation is not a part of the immune system.

text_solutions: Inflammation is an immune response that helps eliminate pathogens and repair damaged tissues.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about vaccines is correct?

options.text: Vaccines stimulate the production of memory cells.
Vaccines do not involve the immune system.

text_solutions: Vaccines stimulate the immune system to produce memory cells, providing long-term immunity.

qns_content.text: Which vaccine is produced using recombinant DNA technology?

text_solutions: The Hepatitis B vaccine is produced using recombinant DNA technology in yeast cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about cytokines is correct?

options.text: Cytokines are signaling molecules that regulate immune responses.
Cytokines are only involved in allergic reactions.
Cytokines only function in the nervous system.

text_solutions: Cytokines are signaling molecules that regulate immune responses, inflammation, and communication between immune cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about leukocytes is incorrect?

options.text: Leukocytes help in defending the body against pathogens.

text_solutions: Leukocytes do not transport oxygen; that function is performed by red blood cells (erythrocytes).

qns_content.text: Which type of immunity is acquired after an infection and subsequent recovery?

text_solutions: Active immunity is acquired after an infection when the immune system produces memory cells for future protection.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a common withdrawal symptom in drug addicts?

text_solutions: Withdrawal symptoms in drug addicts include anxiety, sweating, nausea, and tremors.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of auto-immune diseases?

options.text: The immune system attacks its own cells

text_solutions: Auto-immune diseases occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body’s own cells, as seen in rheumatoid arthritis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about lymphatic vessels is correct?

options.text: Lymphatic vessels absorb fats from the intestine.
Lymphatic vessels have thick muscular walls like arteries.

text_solutions: Lymphatic vessels play a role in fat absorption by transporting dietary fats from the intestines to the bloodstream.

qns_content.text: Which of the following drugs is commonly used for immunosuppression in organ transplantation?

text_solutions: Cyclosporin A is an immunosuppressive drug used to prevent organ transplant rejection.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of passive immunity?

text_solutions: Passive immunity occurs when pre-formed antibodies are directly introduced into the body, such as in tetanus antitoxin administration.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is associated with severe immunosuppression?

text_solutions: AIDS, caused by HIV, leads to severe immunosuppression by destroying CD4+ T-lymphocytes.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a symptom of severe malaria?

text_solutions: Severe malaria can lead to complications such as severe anemia due to the destruction of red blood cells.

qns_content.text: Which organism is responsible for causing amoebiasis?

text_solutions: Amoebiasis is caused by the protozoan Entamoeba histolytica, which infects the human intestine.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about cytokines is incorrect?

options.text: Cytokines are signaling molecules of the immune system.
Cytokines help in cell-to-cell communication during immune responses.

text_solutions: Cytokines do not directly attack pathogens; they mediate immune signaling and coordination.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the lymphatic system is incorrect?

options.text: The lymphatic system helps in immune responses.

text_solutions: Lymphatic vessels do not transport oxygen; they help in immune defense and absorption of fats.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about inflammation is incorrect?

options.text: Inflammation always causes harm to the body.
Inflammation increases blood flow to affected areas.
Inflammation plays a role in tissue repair.

text_solutions: Inflammation is a defense mechanism that helps eliminate pathogens and repair tissues, though excessive inflammation can sometimes be harmful.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about antibodies is incorrect?

options.text: Antibodies recognize and bind to specific antigens.

text_solutions: Antibodies do not directly destroy bacteria; they mark them for destruction by immune cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a toxoid vaccine?

text_solutions: The tetanus vaccine is a toxoid vaccine, meaning it contains an inactivated toxin to stimulate immunity.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is NOT caused by bacteria?

text_solutions: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium, not bacteria.

qns_content.text: Which of the following substances is released by mast cells during an allergic reaction?

text_solutions: Histamine is released by mast cells during allergic reactions, leading to symptoms like swelling and itching.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by a helminthic parasite?

text_solutions: Filariasis is caused by the helminthic parasite Wuchereria bancrofti, which affects the lymphatic system.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the primary mode of transmission for Hepatitis B?

text_solutions: Hepatitis B is primarily transmitted through blood and body fluids, including sexual contact and contaminated needles.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a mode of HIV transmission?

text_solutions: HIV is not transmitted through casual contact such as hugging, shaking hands, or sharing food.

qns_content.text: Which organ is the primary site for T-lymphocyte maturation?

text_solutions: The thymus is the primary site for the maturation of T-lymphocytes, which are crucial for cell-mediated immunity.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a major symptom of ascariasis?

text_solutions: Ascariasis, caused by Ascaris lumbricoides, can lead to intestinal blockage due to excessive worm load.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about lymph nodes is incorrect?

options.text: Lymph nodes filter lymph and trap pathogens.
Lymph nodes contain immune cells like lymphocytes.
Lymph nodes are part of the immune system.

text_solutions: Lymph nodes do not produce red blood cells; their main function is to filter lymph and house immune cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following cells engulf and destroy pathogens in the body?

text_solutions: Macrophages are phagocytic cells that engulf and destroy pathogens as part of innate immunity.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about autoimmune diseases is correct?

options.text: Autoimmune diseases occur when the immune system attacks its own body cells.
Autoimmune diseases are caused by bacterial infections.
Autoimmune diseases occur due to external allergens.
Autoimmune diseases can be treated with antibiotics.

text_solutions: Autoimmune diseases arise when the immune system mistakenly attacks its own cells and tissues.

qns_content.text: Which of the following cells play a major role in allergic reactions?

text_solutions: Mast cells release histamine and other chemicals during allergic reactions.

qns_content.text: Which of the following vaccines is administered orally?

text_solutions: The oral polio vaccine (OPV) is administered orally to provide immunity against poliovirus.

qns_content.text: Which of the following pathogens is transmitted by houseflies?

text_solutions: Houseflies act as mechanical carriers for Entamoeba histolytica, transmitting amoebiasis through contaminated food and water.

qns_content.text: Which substance is responsible for the symptoms of allergy?

text_solutions: Histamine is released by mast cells during allergic reactions, causing symptoms like sneezing, itching, and inflammation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of an autoimmune disease?

text_solutions: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease in which the body's immune system attacks its own tissues, particularly the joints.

qns_content.text: Which disease is diagnosed using the Widal test?

text_solutions: The Widal test is used to diagnose typhoid fever by detecting antibodies against Salmonella typhi.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is prevented by the DPT vaccine?

text_solutions: The DPT vaccine protects against diphtheria, pertussis (whooping cough), and tetanus.

qns_content.text: Which of the following methods is most effective in preventing the spread of cholera?

text_solutions: Cholera is a waterborne disease, and drinking clean, purified water is the most effective way to prevent its spread.

qns_content.text: Which immune cells are responsible for producing histamine in allergic reactions?

text_solutions: Mast cells release histamine, which causes inflammation and other allergic symptoms.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of innate immunity?

text_solutions: Innate immunity includes physical barriers like skin, which prevents the entry of pathogens.

qns_content.text: Which mosquito species is responsible for transmitting dengue fever?

text_solutions: Dengue fever is transmitted by the Aedes mosquito, primarily Aedes aegypti.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about macrophages is incorrect?

text_solutions: Macrophages do not produce antibodies; instead, they engulf pathogens and present antigens to activate other immune cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a viral disease?

text_solutions: The common cold is caused by rhinoviruses, which infect the upper respiratory tract.

qns_content.text: Which of the following conditions is NOT an autoimmune disease?

text_solutions: AIDS is caused by HIV, whereas rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, and multiple sclerosis are autoimmune diseases.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a major symptom of elephantiasis?

text_solutions: Elephantiasis, caused by filarial worms, leads to severe swelling of limbs due to blockage of lymphatic vessels.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a preventive measure for AIDS?

text_solutions: AIDS is mainly transmitted through contaminated needles, sexual contact, and blood transfusions, so using disposable needles helps prevent infection.

qns_content.text: Which chemical is released by virus-infected cells to protect nearby healthy cells?

text_solutions: Interferons are proteins released by virus-infected cells to prevent viral replication in nearby cells.

qns_content.text: Which disease is caused by the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)?

text_solutions: Infectious mononucleosis, also known as the "kissing disease," is caused by the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV).

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about lymph is incorrect?

options.text: Lymph is a fluid that carries white blood cells.
Lymph contains red blood cells for oxygen transport.

text_solutions: Lymph does not contain red blood cells; it carries white blood cells and helps in immune defense.

qns_content.text: What is the function of interferons in the immune system?

text_solutions: Interferons are proteins released by virus-infected cells that protect nearby uninfected cells from viral infections.

qns_content.text: Which type of immunity is provided by a vaccine?

text_solutions: Vaccines stimulate the immune system to develop active acquired immunity by producing memory cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the most effective method to prevent the spread of Hepatitis B?

text_solutions: Hepatitis B is transmitted through contaminated blood, so using disposable syringes helps prevent its spread.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of cancer cells?

text_solutions: Cancer cells lose the property of contact inhibition and undergo uncontrolled cell division, forming tumors.

qns_content.text: Which preventive measure is most effective against air-borne diseases?

options.text: Wearing masks and covering mouth while sneezing

text_solutions: Wearing masks and covering the mouth while sneezing help prevent the spread of air-borne diseases like pneumonia and common cold.

qns_content.text: Which of the following conditions is caused by excessive immune response to harmless antigens?

text_solutions: Allergy occurs when the immune system overreacts to harmless antigens, such as pollen or dust.

qns_content.text: Which immunoglobulin is the first to be produced in response to an infection?

text_solutions: IgM is the first antibody produced during an initial immune response to an infection.

qns_content.text: Which preventive measure is most effective against vector-borne diseases like malaria?

text_solutions: Using mosquito nets, repellents, and eliminating mosquito breeding sites are effective measures against malaria.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the primary site of maturation for B-lymphocytes in humans?

text_solutions: In humans, B-lymphocytes mature in the bone marrow before they participate in immune responses.

qns_content.text: What is the primary function of histamine in allergic reactions?

options.text: Causes vasodilation and increases permeability of blood vessels
Acts as a neurotransmitter in the brain

text_solutions: Histamine is released from mast cells during allergic reactions, leading to vasodilation and increased vascular permeability.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about lymphatic organs is correct?

options.text: The thymus is a secondary lymphoid organ.
Lymph nodes filter pathogens from the blood.
The spleen helps in filtering pathogens from the blood.
The bone marrow does not produce immune cells.

text_solutions: The spleen filters pathogens from the blood and plays an important role in immune defense.

qns_content.text: Which immune cells are responsible for cell-mediated immunity?

text_solutions: T-lymphocytes play a key role in cell-mediated immunity by recognizing and attacking infected or abnormal cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about cancer cells is incorrect?

options.text: Cancer cells lose the ability to undergo controlled cell division.
Cancer cells always remain confined to their original location.
Cancer can be caused by genetic mutations.

text_solutions: Cancer cells can spread to other parts of the body through a process called metastasis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is NOT transmitted through contaminated water?

text_solutions: Dengue is a vector-borne disease transmitted by the Aedes mosquito, not through contaminated water.

qns_content.text: Which hormone stimulates the production of white blood cells?

text_solutions: Thymosin, secreted by the thymus, promotes the development and differentiation of T-lymphocytes.

qns_content.text: Which enzyme helps the HIV virus to integrate its genetic material into the host DNA?

text_solutions: Reverse transcriptase is an enzyme that converts the RNA of HIV into DNA, allowing it to integrate into the host genome.

qns_content.text: Plasmodium, the causative agent of malaria, is transmitted by:

text_solutions: Malaria is transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito, which carries Plasmodium in its salivary glands.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a key function of interferons?

text_solutions: Interferons are proteins that help prevent viral replication and activate immune responses against infections.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a major symptom of scabies?

text_solutions: Scabies is caused by the mite Sarcoptes scabiei and leads to intense itching and rashes on the skin.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a vector-borne disease?

text_solutions: Typhoid is caused by Salmonella typhi and spreads through contaminated food and water, not vectors like mosquitoes.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about immunoglobulin IgA is incorrect?

options.text: IgA is found in mucosal secretions like saliva and tears.
IgA is the most abundant antibody in the bloodstream.
IgA helps prevent pathogen entry at mucosal surfaces.

text_solutions: IgA is primarily found in mucosal secretions and is not the most abundant antibody in the bloodstream; IgG is the most abundant in blood.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about allergic reactions is incorrect?

options.text: Allergic reactions involve the release of histamine.
Mast cells play a major role in allergic reactions.
IgE antibodies are involved in allergic responses.
Allergic reactions are caused by bacterial infections.

text_solutions: Allergic reactions are not caused by bacterial infections but occur due to an overreaction of the immune system to harmless substances.

qns_content.text: Which organ is primarily affected by pneumonia?

text_solutions: Pneumonia affects the alveoli in the lungs, causing inflammation and fluid accumulation, leading to respiratory issues.

qns_content.text: Which type of cancer is characterized by the uncontrolled proliferation of white blood cells?

text_solutions: Leukemia is a type of blood cancer in which abnormal white blood cells multiply uncontrollably.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a common symptom of malaria?

text_solutions: Malaria is characterized by periodic high fever with chills due to the release of toxins by Plasmodium species.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of an antigen-presenting cell (APC)?

text_solutions: Macrophages act as antigen-presenting cells (APCs) by processing and presenting antigens to T-cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about vaccination is incorrect?

options.text: Vaccination stimulates an immune response to create memory cells.

text_solutions: Vaccination provides **active** immunity by stimulating the immune system, not passive immunity.

qns_content.text: Which of the following substances is considered an immunosuppressant?

text_solutions: Cyclosporin A is an immunosuppressant drug that helps prevent organ transplant rejection.

qns_content.text: Which disease is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis?

text_solutions: Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and primarily affects the lungs.

qns_content.text: Which class of immunoglobulin is responsible for allergic reactions?

text_solutions: IgE antibodies are involved in allergic reactions by triggering the release of histamines from mast cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about cancer is TRUE?

text_solutions: Malignant tumors exhibit metastasis, meaning they spread to distant organs through the blood or lymph.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?

text_solutions: AIDS is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), which attacks the immune system.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about malaria is incorrect?

options.text: Malaria can be prevented by eliminating mosquito breeding sites.

text_solutions: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium, a protozoan, and not by bacteria.

qns_content.text: Which disease is characterized by severe muscle spasms and lockjaw?

text_solutions: Tetanus is caused by Clostridium tetani and is characterized by severe muscle stiffness and lockjaw.

qns_content.text: Which of the following pathogens causes typhoid fever in humans?

text_solutions: Typhoid fever is caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi, which spreads through contaminated food and water.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a live-attenuated vaccine?

text_solutions: The oral polio vaccine contains live-attenuated poliovirus, which helps induce immunity without causing disease.

qns_content.text: Which immunoglobulin is primarily involved in allergic reactions?

text_solutions: IgE antibodies trigger allergic reactions by binding to mast cells and causing histamine release.

qns_content.text: Which disease is associated with abnormal proliferation of lymphocytes?

text_solutions: Leukemia is a type of blood cancer characterized by uncontrolled proliferation of abnormal lymphocytes.

qns_content.text: Which immune component is responsible for transplant rejection?

text_solutions: T-lymphocytes play a key role in transplant rejection by recognizing foreign tissues as non-self and attacking them.

qns_content.text: Which part of the immune system is responsible for the production of antibodies?

text_solutions: B-lymphocytes produce antibodies as part of the humoral immune response.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about phagocytes is incorrect?

options.text: Phagocytes help in engulfing and digesting pathogens.
Neutrophils and macrophages are examples of phagocytes.
Phagocytosis is a key process in innate immunity.

text_solutions: Phagocytes do not secrete antibodies; instead, they engulf and digest pathogens as part of the innate immune response.

qns_content.text: Which component of the immune system is responsible for long-term immunity?

text_solutions: Memory B-cells provide long-term immunity by recognizing and responding to previously encountered pathogens.

qns_content.text: Which of the following drugs is classified as an opioid?

text_solutions: Heroin is an opioid drug derived from morphine and acts as a depressant on the central nervous system.

qns_content.text: Which type of vaccine contains weakened live pathogens?

text_solutions: Live-attenuated vaccines contain weakened pathogens that stimulate an immune response without causing disease.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about neutrophils is incorrect?

options.text: Neutrophils are a type of white blood cell.

text_solutions: Neutrophils do not produce antibodies; instead, they engulf and destroy pathogens through phagocytosis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about T-helper cells is correct?

options.text: T-helper cells function in the innate immune response.

text_solutions: T-helper cells (CD4+ T-cells) activate B-cells and cytotoxic T-cells to enhance immune responses.

qns_content.text: Which test is used for the diagnosis of typhoid fever?

text_solutions: The Widal test is a serological test used to diagnose typhoid fever by detecting antibodies against Salmonella typhi.

qns_content.text: Which immune response involves the activation of antibodies against a pathogen?

text_solutions: Humoral immunity involves the production of antibodies by B-cells to neutralize pathogens.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by a helminth parasite?

text_solutions: Filariasis is caused by the helminth Wuchereria, which affects the lymphatic system.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about active immunity is incorrect?

options.text: Active immunity develops after exposure to an antigen.
Active immunity is short-lived and does not last long.

text_solutions: Active immunity provides long-lasting protection because it involves the formation of memory cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the site of maturation for B-lymphocytes in humans?

text_solutions: In humans, B-lymphocytes mature in the bone marrow before they circulate in the immune system.

qns_content.text: Which of the following acts as a physical barrier in innate immunity?

text_solutions: Skin is a physical barrier that prevents the entry of pathogens into the body.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is spread by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito?

text_solutions: Malaria is transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito, which carries Plasmodium.

qns_content.text: Which type of immunity is acquired by recovering from a disease?

text_solutions: Active acquired immunity develops when the immune system produces antibodies in response to an infection.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about antigen-antibody interactions is incorrect?

options.text: Antibodies bind to specific antigens to neutralize them.
Antigens are produced by the immune system.

text_solutions: Antigens are foreign substances (like pathogens or toxins) that stimulate an immune response; they are not produced by the immune system.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about immunological memory is correct?

options.text: Immunological memory is a characteristic of innate immunity.
Memory cells help provide faster immune responses upon re-exposure to the same pathogen.

text_solutions: Memory cells, formed during an initial infection, enable the immune system to respond faster and more effectively upon re-exposure to the same pathogen.
